title: Cocontinuous unary change of enrichment on algebroids
statement:
Let $V,W$ be cocomplete monoidal infinity categories whose tensors preserve small colimits separately, with algebroids as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The infinity categories $\operatorname{Algd}(V)$ and $\operatorname{Algd}(W)$ admit small colimits. If $F:V\to W$ is strong monoidal and preserves small colimits, composition of operadic algebras with $F$ defines $F_*:\operatorname{Algd}(V)\to\operatorname{Algd}(W)$, and this functor preserves small colimits. Explicitly, for every small infinity category $K$ and diagram $A:K\to\operatorname{Algd}(V)$, the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}F_*A_k\longrightarrow F_*(\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}A_k)$$
is an equivalence. This includes the empty diagram. No presentability hypothesis on $V,W$ is assumed.

source.place: Observation 3.9; Gepner-Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, Proposition 3.6.10 and section 4.3 (in particular Proposition 4.3.14); online source, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Use the object-space projection $p_{\mathcal V}:\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\to\mathcal S$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration], which is a Cartesian (hence inner) fibration for any monoidal $\mathcal V$. Its fiber is $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$, and its mapping-space homotopy fiber over $f:X\to Y$ is $\operatorname{Map}(A,f^*B)$. The same cited statement constructs postcomposition by $F$ as a functor $F_*$ over $\mathcal S$ commuting coherently with restriction. Thus its object space is unchanged and its fiber functor $H_X$ is postcomposition on algebras. No cocontinuity assertion is being taken from this node.

source.place: Definitions 3.6.1, 3.6.12 and 4.3.1; Lemma 4.3.9. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $q(X)=L_{\mathrm{gen}}\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$. The natural equivalence of [lem-coef-many-object-operad-accessibility] identifies $\operatorname{Alg}_{q(X)}(\mathcal V)$ with $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$, for every monoidal $\mathcal V$. It commutes with restriction in $X$ and postcomposition in $\mathcal V$: both are composition with the same unit $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to q(X)$. Each $q(X)$ is a small ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad; by the Segal condition at $[0]$ in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], its zero-fiber is contractible. Consequently for every $f:X\to Y$, $q(f)$ is an equivalence on zero-fibers and satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions]. Apply that node to $q(f)$, and transport its adjunction along these natural equivalences, obtaining $f_!^{\mathcal V}\dashv f^*$. Also [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change] applied to $q(X)$ gives all small fiber colimits, and says that each $H_X$ preserves them. These applications use only cocompleteness and separate tensor cocontinuity, not presentability. We use $q(f)$ here, not $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_Y^{\mathrm{op}}$, whose zero-fiber map need not be an equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.14; Remark 4.3.2; Theorem A.4.6; Corollary A.5.7; Proposition A.5.10. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
For $A$ in the fiber over $X$, use the unit $A\to f^*f_!^{\mathcal V}A$ to form the arrow $A\to f_!^{\mathcal V}A$ over $f:X\to Y$ in the total category. This is cocartesian. Indeed, for a test object $C$ over $Z$ and a map $g:Y\to Z$, the homotopy fibers over $g$ of its mapping-space comparison are, by [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration], respectively $\operatorname{Map}(f_!^{\mathcal V}A,g^*C)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(A,f^*g^*C)$. Precomposition with this unit identifies them by the adjunction in [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions]; the identifications are natural in $g,C$. Comparing the mapping square to its homotopy pullback over $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(Y,Z)$, apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with the identity on that base: the comparison is an equivalence because it is so on every homotopy fiber. This proves exactly the cocartesian mapping-square criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits]. Together with the inner-fibration property in step 1, it makes $p_{\mathcal V}$ a cocartesian fibration with transport $f_!^{\mathcal V}$. The argument applies equally to $\mathcal W$. Each transport preserves all small colimits, by the following universal-property argument. The dual coherent-adjunction assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] applied to $f^*$ and its unit extends the adjunction to $K$-diagram functor categories. For a small fiber diagram $B$, write $\ell=\operatorname{colim} B$, whose existence follows from [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change]. For every target $C$, the adjunction, the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and the coherent-diagram adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Map}(f_!\ell,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\ell,f^*C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_X)}(B,\operatorname{const}(f^*C))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_Y)}(f_!B,\operatorname{const}(C)).$$
All three maps are the specified precomposition maps from the unit and the image cocone. The dual cocone criterion therefore says that $f_!\ell$ with this cocone is a colimit of $f_!B$. This proves transport cocontinuity, including the empty diagram, without assuming a pointwise formula for algebra colimits.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.6 and the mapping-space definition of cocartesian arrows; Proposition A.4.3. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED. Generic coherent-adjunction and cocone mapping criteria are supplied by the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: The base $\mathcal S$ admits all small colimits: [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] states that spaces are presentable and every presentable infinity category has small colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits] to the cocartesian fibrations of step 3 and the cocomplete fibers of step 2. This proves both total categories are cocomplete and gives the actual colimit cocones. More explicitly, for the given small $K$-diagram $A$, put $X=\operatorname{colim}_K X_k$ with cocone $f_k:X_k\to X$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to its coherent base transformation to the constant diagram at $X$. The resulting transported diagram $D$ lies in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V))$, with $D_k=f_{k,!}^{\mathcal V}A_k$ and a coherent cocartesian transformation $A\to D$. Thus it is a coherent diagram, not just the list of transported objects. The total-colimit formula says that $L=\operatorname{colim}^{\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)}_K D$ equipped with the composite cocone from $A$ is a colimit of $A$ in $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.9 and Lemma 4.3.7; the cocartesian total-category colimit formula used there. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
For every $f:X\to Y$, apply the coefficient-change mate of [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions] to $q(f)$, as justified in step 2. It yields a natural equivalence
$$f_!^{\mathcal W}H_X\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Yf_!^{\mathcal V}.$$
Its defining unit formula says that the image under $F_*$ of the cocartesian unit arrow $A\to f_!^{\mathcal V}A$ is the $\mathcal W$-cocartesian unit arrow $H_XA\to f_!^{\mathcal W}H_XA$ followed by this equivalence in the fiber over $Y$. It is therefore cocartesian: precomposition by a fiber equivalence leaves the mapping-space pullback criterion unchanged. Any other cocartesian lift over $f$ with the same source has the same mapping-space universal property: the two properties give maps between the targets over the identity of $Y$, and their composites are homotopic to the respective identities by uniqueness in those mapping-space fibers. Hence their targets are equivalent in the fiber. It follows that $F_*$ preserves all cocartesian arrows. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to the transformation $A\to D$ from step 4. Its image $F_*A\to H_XD$ has cocartesian components, and hence is a cocartesian lift of the same coherent base transformation. The cited node's coherent transport and mapping-space formula identify the transported diagram for $F_*A$ with $H_XD$, including its cocone from $F_*A$. Thus the equivalences here identify transformations and their higher simplices, not just object values.

source.place: Lemma A.4.7 and the proof of Proposition 3.6.10. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change], the fiber functor $H_X$ preserves the $K$-colimit of $D$; hence the canonical fiber comparison $\operatorname{colim}^{\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal W)}_K H_XD\to H_XL$ is an equivalence compatible with the fiber cocone. The formula of [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits], using the coherent transported diagram identified in step 5, identifies its source with $\operatorname{colim}_K F_*A$. Its target, regarded in the total category over $X$, is $F_*L$. The compatibility with the transported cocones shows that this arrow is precisely the canonical comparison in the item. For $K$ empty the base colimit is $X=\varnothing$, the transported diagram is empty, and the same fiber theorem sends its initial object to the initial object in the fiber over $\varnothing$. The total-colimit formula then makes the comparison an equivalence for the empty diagram too. This proves every asserted colimit preservation statement under the original hypotheses.
